description: Divergences from the pinned Python reference (rns==0.9.5, lxmf==0.7.0) that conformance/fuzz/run-differential.mjs is allowed to observe. Any kind not listed here fails the `differential-fuzz` gate and its input is written to conformance/vectors/fuzz-regressions.json. A kind is `<target>:<direction>:<reason>`; `ts-accepts` means we parsed a frame the reference refused, which is the direction that carries security weight and should be treated as a bug unless there is a reason here that says otherwise.

allowances.reason: `msgpackUnpack` is a deliberate subset of msgpack, not a general decoder: it implements nil, positive fixint, uint8/16/32, float64, bin8/16, fixarray and fixmap, which is everything LXMF and RNS resource advertisements actually put on the wire. It has no str, bool, negative int, int8/16/64, float32, array16/32, map16/32, bin32 or ext. Every tag outside that set is refused, and `umsgpack` decodes it. This is the safe direction — we reject what the reference accepts, so the failure mode is dropping a frame no peer sends rather than parsing one we do not understand. Narrowing the subset is a decoder change, not a fuzz finding; widening it would need each new type to have a call site.

We type-check advertisement fields and RNS does not. `ResourceAdvertisement.unpack` there assigns whatever msgpack produced straight onto the object, so `{"f": -1}` becomes a flags byte of -1 and `{"q": {}}` becomes a request id that is a dict; both then flow into the resource state machine. We require `t`/`d`/`n`/`f`/`i`/`l` to be msgpack ints, `h`/`r`/`o`/`m` to be bins, and `q` to be a bin or nil, and reject otherwise. Same safe direction as above: a frame RNS would mis-handle is one we decline to build a resource from.
